source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Air Injection Reactor System, p.6T-5

procedures.title: A.I.R. air injection tubes: inspect and replace
steps: V8: clamp the exhaust manifold in a vise, clean the carbon off the tubes and work them out of the manifold using penetrating oil.
Fit new tubes in the manifold.

procedures.title: A.I.R. pump: inspect
steps: Run the engine up to about 1500 rpm and feel the air flow from the hoses; if it increases with speed the pump is working.
If flow is missing or does not increase, check belt tension and look for a leaking pressure relief valve (it can be heard with the pump running).
For excessive noise, run the engine with the pump belt off; if the noise remains, it is not the A.I.R. system.
If the noise goes away with the belt off, check for a seized pump, leaks or bad routing at hoses, tubes, air manifolds and connections, and proper pump mounting.
If none of these is found and the pump is still too noisy, replace the pump.
notes: The system is never fully silent; normal noise rises in pitch with engine speed.

procedures.title: A.I.R. pump: replace
steps: Disconnect the hoses at the pump.
Remove the mounting bolts and the pump.
Fit the new pump with its mounting bolts loose.

procedures.title: A.I.R. pressure relief valve: replace
steps: Pull the relief valve from the housing with J-7055-5 and J-6585 (see figure 8 in the manual).
Tap the new valve in with a 15/16" socket until it shoulders on the housing (see figure 9 in the manual), taking great care not to distort the housing.
notes: If the relief valve is built into the diverter valve, replace the whole diverter valve unit.
